a2-unit-33.33.1 Who's behind the wheel?:
Reporter: Who's behind the wheel? The future of self-driving cars.
Reporter: Is your drive to work a waste of time? Maybe you hate driving, or you don't have a driver's license. For many people, the answer is the self-driving car. Carmakers and tech companies have made many predictions about when this technology will be ready.
Reporter: Experts describe six levels of driving automation, from Level zero to Level five. At the lowest levels, the driver controls the car, and the computer helps with parking or staying in a lane. This technology is already in many new cars. At Level five, the computer is in control everywhere, and the driver is free to work or sleep. Most experts predict that Level five cars won't be available for many years.
Reporter: But driverless taxis are already here. The company Waymo now runs robotaxis in more than ten American cities, including Phoenix, Los Angeles, Atlanta and Orlando. "The first time, I was a little scared," says Carol, a Brazilian who lives in Orlando. "Now I think it's probably safer than my own driving!"
Reporter: Are self-driving cars safe? About thirty-nine thousand people died in crashes on American roads in twenty twenty-four, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Self-driving cars might prevent thousands of these accidents, although drivers could become too confident about the technology. Self-driving cars will have other effects, too. They will probably be better for the environment, because a computer drives more efficiently than a person.
Reporter: Self-driving cars may replace many taxis and delivery vans, and it will certainly be cheaper to run a taxi company with no drivers to pay. If robotaxis become really popular, this might result in big changes in the number of people who want to own a car. The biggest winners are likely to be older people who don't feel confident on busy roads, and some people with disabilities who can't drive.
Reporter: The question isn't if we will see self-driving cars everywhere. It's when.
